title: Hedge Completeness for Context-Setting Interventions with Selector Variables
banked_reason: D0.5 rejected the headline: the proposed terminal trace violates mandatory LS-ADMMG label deletion, the prompt uses the wrong SS-ID target semantics, and no universal cs_fail_2 certificate was proved.
gap_reasons: forced_label_deletion: each eligible A_0-serious context deletes the required labelled S→A_0 edge, so the asserted line-9 trace instead has a valid Algorithm 2 candidate.
target-functional-mismatch: the prompt and stale core metadata use a natural S=empty event with a pi(empty) factor, whereas SS-ID targets do(A=a,S=empty).
novelty-floor-unmet: no generic final-return family or universal cs_fail_2 certificate was proved.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a restricted parity cancellation lemma, then attempted to turn a four-vertex support-pooling construction into an identified Algorithm 2 line-9 failure. D0.5 refuted that trace because mandatory selector-edge labels are deleted in every eligible serious context, yielding a valid candidate instead. The published SS-ID completeness conjecture therefore remains open.
tldr: The completeness program is reversed. The exact \(\mathsf{SS\text{-}ID}\) target is the context-setting intervention \(p(X_Y(a,S=\emptyset))\), and the input is the full observed joint law \(p(X_{V^\circ},S)\). A support-pooling family reaches the final bare return of Algorithm 2 even though every positive selector stratum implements \(A=a\), so the target is identified by the observed marginal \(p(X_Y)\). Thus the final return is not a universal nonidentification certificate: the published algorithm remains sound but is not complete. The two-arm parity calculation is retained only as a supporting cancellation and normalization check.
gap: Algorithm 2 searches for one supported selector context that simultaneously passes a context-specific independence test and a fixing-reachability test. It does not pool selector strata that all implement the same intervention. Consequently its final return can occur at an identified query.
fill: If all positive selector states seriously assign \(A=a\), do not seriously assign target ancestors downstream of \(A\), and \(A\) cuts every directed path from \(S\) to those ancestors, then \(X_Y(a,S=\emptyset)=X_Y\) almost surely and the identifying functional is \(p(X_Y)\). A four-vertex LS-ADMMG satisfies these conditions and reaches the final Algorithm 2 failure, refuting the completeness conjecture and motivating a support-pooling precheck.
